what_happened: Job 20261030-113229-kgrg (code job: record kill-switch-stopped jobs as stopped and resumable, not failed) failed in planning before any code was written. The planner hit its fixed 600-second deadline without finishing. The event lists no critic findings, no unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks. Nothing was delivered, and no partial plan or reason was kept.
cause: The planner has a fixed 600s wall-clock deadline. It keeps no partial plan, gives no progress signal and has no resume or retry. Nothing sizes the request against that deadline before planning starts, and nothing records what the planner was doing when time ran out. The request touches job lifecycle states (stopped vs failed, resumability), which probably spans several surfaces (state model, kill-switch handling, status output, retry). A deadline stop throws away all planning spend and gives no diagnosis. This is the second case in a day with the same outcome.
other_causes: The request may bundle several changes (a new state, resume behavior, and status reporting), so planning was larger than one round could finish.
open_hypotheses: The request may have been too large for 600s, but the fields do not show the plan's size or what the planner was doing.
The planner may have stalled on reading code about the kill switch or job states. The fields cannot confirm this.
The deadline may be too short for this role in general, not for this job.
contradictions: The request is a single, apparently well-bounded state-labelling change, which points against it being oversized.
prevention: Make the planner stage keep partial output and report progress. Persist the draft plan and the last activity at each step. On a deadline stop, hold the job as resumable with that draft instead of failing it, and record the reason. Check the request's size against the deadline before dispatch and split it when it is too large. This would prevent the whole class, including the earlier case 20261114-052207-pj25.
proposed_request: When the planner stage reaches its time deadline, Athena should not end the job as failed with nothing kept. Outcome: (1) the planner writes its draft plan and a short note of what it was doing to the job's records as it works; (2) on a deadline stop the job is held as stopped and resumable, with the draft and the reason shown in `athena status`; (3) `athena retry` on such a job resumes planning from the draft, not from scratch; (4) a test demonstrates a planner that exceeds the deadline leaves a resumable job with a kept draft and a recorded reason. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
